subject: Clarification and proposed appendix: ownership of edge/NAT latency for private VPC
messages:
From: David Liu <david.liu@stellarnet.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stellarnet.com>, Ops Team <ops@stellarnet.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Question on SLA coverage for customer edge devices (private VPC)

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're lining up legal + network to finish the Private deployment SOW and there is one outstanding ask from NOC: can Redwood confirm how uptime/latency commitments apply when traffic traverses customer-managed edge appliances (NAT, firewall, load balancer) in our colo? Specifically:

- If StellarNet's edge appliance introduces persistent latency spikes or packet drops that only affect the last hop (inside our colo), will that be treated as a Redwood SLA violation?
- What type of evidence will Redwood expect to demonstrate that an incident was due to customer-managed infrastructure versus Redwood runtime?

I've attached a simple diagram of our proposed edge placement. Procurement would like the language to be explicit (we're trying to avoid a later dispute).

Appreciate a short note on how you typically handle this.

Best,
David
David Liu
Head of Infrastructure, StellarNet

Attachment: stellarnet-edge-network-diagram.pdf
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: David Liu <david.liu@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on SLA coverage for customer edge devices (private VPC)

Hi David — thanks for the diagram, that helps. Short answer: Redwood's hosted runtime SLA only covers the service components we operate (compute, model serving, control plane) and the network hops we control. For Private/VPC/on-prem deployments, we exclude customer-managed edge/network devices from our uptime/latency obligations, but we also try to be pragmatic about investigative tooling and evidence.

Proposed practical approach (we can bake into an appendix):
1) Exclusion clause: explicit language that latency/availability attributable to customer-controlled appliances (NAT, FW, edge LB, colo transit) are excluded from Redwood SLA calculations.
2) Evidence standard: dual-sided measurements —
   - Redwood will provide server-side telemetry (token latency, gRPC traces, kernel-level egress times).
   - Customer will provide colocation/edge device logs or packet captures showing increased latency or drops across the customer hop.
3) Measurement windows: define the measurement endpoint pair (Redwood egress -> customer ingress) and use synchronized timestamps / NTP to correlate.
4) Escalation path: if evidence is inconclusive, we propose a neutral third-party packet capture review (cost split TBD) or a 48h joint war room to root cause.

I'll draft suggested appendix language and send for legal review. Naomi/Vanessa — tagging you to confirm this aligns with our precedent and evidence requirements.

If that's acceptable, we can circulate a short diff to the SOW.

- Logan
Logan Wright
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 May 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on SLA coverage for customer edge devices (private VPC)

Quick notes from legal/ops perspective:
- Legal: We should keep exclusion succinct and avoid introducing a broad "we're not responsible for anything outside our cloud" phrasing. Instead, limit to "customer-managed physical/virtual edge appliances and customer-owned last-mile connectivity."
- Ops: For evidence, we require at minimum: server-side latency histogram, request IDs with timestamps, and either customer packet captures or switch port counters showing loss. If customer refuses to provide logs, treat as inconclusive; the neutral review option is necessary.

I drafted a one-paragraph appendix (attached as a Word diff) that mirrors what Logan suggested but with tightened language for contracts. We should also include an operational checklist (who runs capture, how to exchange artifacts securely).

Attachment: proposed-sla-appendix-diff.docx

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: David Liu <david.liu@stellarnet.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on SLA coverage for customer edge devices (private VPC)

David / StellarNet team — thanks for raising this. We reviewed your diagram and Naomi + I worked with Legal to produce the attached appendix language. High level:

- Redwood will exclude customer-managed edge infrastructure from SLA calculations when the root cause is demonstrated to be within the customer hop.
- Required evidence: Redwood server-side traces + at least one of (customer packet capture showing increased latency/loss, colo switch port loss counters, or historical telemetry from the customer's edge appliance).
- If evidence is inconclusive, Redwood and StellarNet will engage a neutral third party for packet capture analysis; cost-sharing to be negotiated in the SOW addendum.
- For operational clarity we propose a 48h joint incident window and an exchange-of-artifacts checklist (we included the checklist in the attachment).

Next steps: please review the attached diff and indicate whether Procurement is comfortable with the neutral-review cost share line (we proposed 50/50 for parties when both sides request it). If you accept, we'll send the appendix to your counsel and include the reference in the SOW exhibit.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-sla-appendix-diff.docx
